lines.trans: How do you leave your phone lying around like this every single day?
A call just came in from the guy your colleague offered to set you up with yesterday.
Did you answer it?
Nope—I turned him down. Call him back yourself if you want.
Listen, a man can tell another man right away!
All that talk about liking fierce women and stylish outfits—just hearing the description, that guy is bad news.
How funny—yesterday Seung-chan said the exact same thing you just said.
Baek Seung-chan did?
Yeah, saying that guy sounded questionable! If two men say the exact same thing, that guy really must be no good, right?

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그 아이 ('that child/kid'); used only for younger people or close peers.

examples.trans: Are you close with her?
He is late every day.

related.gloss: this kid / he or she (near speaker)
that kid / he or she (over there)

meanings.note: Used as casual past (거절했어.).

examples.text: 아니, 거절했어. 뭐 네가 다시 하든가.
examples.trans: Nope—I turned him down. Call him back yourself if you want.
Let us do that (I turned him down) right away.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.
Did you hear about this man?
I was busy today because of man.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children

meanings.en: to go around, to attend, to commute
meanings.note: Indicates regular movement or carrying something around constantly.

examples.trans: I commute to the company.
I carry a bag around with me.

meanings.note: repeating an action or returning to a previous state

examples.trans: Please say that one more time.
I'll come back in a moment.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

meanings.note: Attributive form of 둘 used directly before counter nouns (두 개, 두 사람).

examples.trans: Please give me two apples.
Let's meet at two o'clock.

meanings.note: Used as bound noun (둥).

examples.text: 신디야, 네가 피디랑 몸싸움을 하다가 다쳤다는 둥 별 말 같지도 않은 말들이 떠도는 모양이야.
examples.trans: Cindy, absurd rumors seem to be floating around claiming you got hurt scuffling with a producer.
This point about rumors saying things like is really important.

meanings.note: verb listen

examples.trans: Listen well.

examples.trans: How funny—yesterday Seung-chan said the exact same thing you just said.

examples.text: 응, 그 남자는 좀 아닌 것 같다면서! 두 남자가 똑같은 소리를 한다는 건 그 남자가 진짜 아니라는 얘기지?

meanings.en: always, all the time, every day
meanings.note: colloquial pronunciation/variant of 만날; often carries mild exasperation

examples.trans: He always comes late.
Why do you make the same mistake every time?

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: Used for gifts, money, messages, or documents.

examples.trans: I received a birthday present.
Please answer the phone.

meanings.note: Refers to the immediate past.

examples.trans: I arrived just now.
What did you just say?

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Can refer to a single person or people/a crowd in general without a plural suffix.

examples.trans: There are many people in the cafeteria.
He is a good person.
It really is strongly, boldly compared to what I thought.
Especially today, it is strongly, boldly and nice.

examples.trans: It is not my fault.

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
